# Automated canonical union and publication

Publish certified merge runs on every push to main and on manual dispatch, using only trusted main code and the repository GITHUB_TOKEN. It first certifies the initial canonical in both literal and actual pandas 3.1.0 modes, runs the ordinary union over every poc/*/final.csv, and independently checks all 1000 final groups against that initial snapshot. Both modes must have zero per-n regressions, the same strictly improved groups, and a strictly smaller official total score before changed canonical bytes can be committed. Unchanged bytes produce no main commit. Failed gates stop publication. No geometry cache is restored.

Only the canonical file is committed, with koboshchan author and committer identity. GITHUB_TOKEN pushes do not trigger recursive push workflows; an additional narrow exact single-automation-commit guard does not skip manual dispatch or mixed real pushes. Certification uses a clean latest-main checkout; any main advancement invalidates the run. The normal fast-forward mirror push atomically guards the exact source main SHA, including when that SHA is a newly created union commit. The merge branch retains exactly one score-named CSV with the certified canonical bytes. No force push is used.

Publisher gates and disposable local Git integration tests are in .github/scripts/test_publish_certified_merge.py. They cover strict gains, no-ops, invalid reports, self-commit filtering, canonical-only commits, exact mirror bytes/filename, and concurrent-main rejection. They never fabricate or submit a real packing.
